data.cultural_impact: Anirvan is a rare Sanskrit name found in Hindu literature and mythology. It is a name synonymous with the ultimate goal of human life in Hinduism - moksha or liberation. The name Anirvan is mentioned in the ancient Hindu scriptures, especially the Bhagavad Gita, as a synonym for the enlightened soul or the person who has realized the self beyond the material world and has transcended the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth to attain salvation. This name holds immense cultural significance in India, where the pursuit of spiritual growth and self-realization is deeply ingrained in society and history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Anirvan holds significant spiritual importance in Hinduism. It symbolizes the ultimate goal of human life - the attainment of moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words "anir" meaning "endless" and "van" meaning "goal" or "destination". Thus, Anirvan means "one who is beyond the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth". This name is an embodiment of the ideal of self-realization and spiritual growth pursued in Hinduism. It signifies the ultimate freedom from the material world and the attainment of pure, infinite consciousness - a powerful reminder of the ultimate purpose and goal of human life.

historical_references.reference: Anirvan is a name of a Hindu monk and philosopher, also known as Shri Shri Shankaradeva, who lived during the 15th century in Assam, India. He is considered a major figure in the Vaishnavism tradition and is known for his teachings on the Bhagavad Gita and the philosophy of love and devotion (bhakti) towards Vishnu.

historical_references.reference: Anirvan is also the name of a prominent Hindu saint and reformer from medieval Bengal, India. He lived during the late 16th and early 17th centuries and is known for his works on Advaita Vedanta philosophy and his efforts to reform Hindu society.
